bib.title: You Only Cache Once: Decoder-Decoder Architectures for Language Models

question: Can a decoder-decoder architecture that caches global key-value pairs once cut KV memory and prefill time at long context while matching a Transformer's quality?
hypothesis: Reusing one global KV cache from a self-decoder in all cross-decoder layers keeps global attention and allows prefill to exit early, with competitive language modeling.
contributions: Decoder-decoder architecture YOCO (self-decoder plus cross-decoder) that caches KV once
Gated retention as the efficient self-attention module
Scaling in tokens (1.6T), size (160M-13B) and context (1M)
Profiling showing orders-of-magnitude gains in memory, prefill latency and throughput

method.summary: YOCO stacks L/2 self-decoder layers (gated retention or sliding-window attention, constant cache) under L/2 cross-decoder layers that all cross-attend to one global KV cache projected from the self-decoder output. Prefill can exit before the cross-decoder. A 3B model is trained to 1.6T tokens, extended to 1M context, and profiled against a GQA Transformer.
method.task: autoregressive language model pretraining and long-context inference profiling

datasets.name: curated training corpus similar to StableLM-3B-4E1T
datasets.size: 1.6T tokens (3B model); 10B tokens per scaling-curve model
datasets.preprocessing: tiktoken-cl100k_base tokenizer; long documents up-sampled by sequence length for length extension

datasets.name: LM Eval Harness tasks (ARC-C, ARC-E, BoolQ, HellaSwag, OBQA, PIQA, Winogrande, SciQ)
Needle In A Haystack and multi-needle
datasets.preprocessing: needle is a city with a magic number

datasets.name: Book and repository-level code validation data
ZeroSCROLLS (Qasper, GovReport, QMSum, NarrativeQA)
datasets.preprocessing: 160M models trained 2B more tokens at 16,384 length

models.name: YOCO scaling series (gRet, SWA)
models.architecture: as above; SWA window 1,024; gRet head dim 256

models.name: Llama-style Transformer (scaling and profiling baseline)
models.architecture: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, no bias; GQA, Flash-Decoding, kernel fusion in profiling

other.note: StableLM-3B-4E1T numbers taken from its technical report

training.optimizer: AdamW, betas (0.9, 0.95) for 3B; (0.9, 0.98) for scaling curves
training.lr: 3.2e-4 max for 3B; 1.5e-4 (160M-1.4B) and 7.5e-5 (2.7B-13B) for scaling curves; 8e-5, 4e-5, 2e-5 for length stages
training.lr_schedule: linear decay to 1.28e-5 over a 5T-token schedule (3B); linear decay (scaling curves)
training.batch_size: 4M tokens (3B); 0.25M tokens (scaling curves); same as before for length extension
training.tokens: 1.6T (3B); 10B per scaling-curve model; 6B + 4B + 1.5B for length extension

other.kernel: Triton gated retention kernel based on FLA
other.long_context_training: chunk parallelism (Appendix A), internal CUBE system

inference.samples: needle test: 10 runs at the same depth and length, averaged; profiling runs not stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot for Eval Harness; no long-instruction tuning data

parameters.hardware: H100-80GB GPU cards (count not stated for 3B profiling)
parameters.prefill_mode: chunk-recurrent for gRet; generation uses recurrent form

metrics.name: needle retrieval accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of needles retrieved, mean of 10 runs

metrics.name: validation loss / perplexity
metrics.definition: LM loss on held-out validation set

metrics.name: prefilling latency
metrics.definition: encoding time of the prompt before first token

metrics.name: throughput
metrics.definition: tokens per second including prefill and generation

baselines: Llama-style Transformer with GQA, Flash-Decoding, kernel fusion
H3, RetNet, Mamba, gRetNet, Sparse Transformer (Appendix G)
eval.protocol: single training run per configuration; no seeds or significance tests reported

evidence.quote: The experiments are conducted with H100-80GB GPU cards.

results.claim: Whole-model inference memory at 1M context is 12.4GB for YOCO, with the Transformer using 9.4x more.
results.setup: YOCO-gRet 3B (26 layers, 24 query heads, 8 KV heads, GQA) vs same-size Transformer with GQA, Flash-Decoding and kernel fusion; H100-80GB; last 1,024 tokens generated; Section 4.4
results.quote: For example of 1M length, the overall inference memory usage is only 12.4GB, while Transformers occupy 9.4× GPU memory.

results.claim: At 32K context YOCO needs about 2x less memory than the Transformer.
results.setup: YOCO-gRet 3B (26 layers, 24 query heads, 8 KV heads, GQA) vs same-size Transformer with GQA, Flash-Decoding and kernel fusion; H100-80GB; last 1,024 tokens generated; Section 4.4
results.quote: Even with a 32K sequence length, YOCO requires about 2× less memory than Transformer.

results.claim: Prefill for a 512K context drops from 180 seconds to under 6 seconds.
results.setup: YOCO-gRet 3B (26 layers, 24 query heads, 8 KV heads, GQA) vs same-size Transformer with GQA, Flash-Decoding and kernel fusion; H100-80GB; last 1,024 tokens generated; Section 4.4; 512K prefill
results.quote: Figure 9 shows that YOCO reduces the Transformer prefilling time from 180 seconds to less than 6 seconds for 512K context.

results.claim: Prefill is 71.8x faster at 1M and 2.87x faster at 32K.
results.setup: YOCO-gRet 3B (26 layers, 24 query heads, 8 KV heads, GQA) vs same-size Transformer with GQA, Flash-Decoding and kernel fusion; H100-80GB; last 1,024 tokens generated; Section 4.4
results.quote: The prefill stage is speeded up by 71.8× for the 1M context and 2.87× for the 32K input.

results.setup: YOCO-gRet 3B (26 layers, 24 query heads, 8 KV heads, GQA) vs same-size Transformer with GQA, Flash-Decoding and kernel fusion; H100-80GB; last 1,024 tokens generated; Section 4.4

results.claim: Throughput at 512K context is 43.1 token/s for YOCO against 4.5 for the Transformer, 9.6x.
results.setup: YOCO-gRet 3B (26 layers, 24 query heads, 8 KV heads, GQA) vs same-size Transformer with GQA, Flash-Decoding and kernel fusion; H100-80GB; last 1,024 tokens generated; Section 4.4; throughput covers prefill plus generation; larger batch allowed by lower memory
results.quote: For the example of 512K queries, Transformer’s throughput is 4.5 token/s while YOCO reaches 43.1 token/s, i.e, achieving 9.6× speedup.

results.claim: KV cache per token is reduced about 80x at 65B.
results.setup: KV cache KB/token vs model size 1.2B-65B; Transformer baseline uses GQA; Fig 8 labels 24x/32x/40x/64x/80x; the 65B figure is read from per-token cost, not a measured run
results.quote: In particular, the memory of KV caches can be reduced by about 80× for 65B models.

results.claim: At 65B YOCO can serve 128K tokens in 1GB of GPU memory, against 1.6K tokens for a GQA Transformer.
results.setup: 65B model size, per-token KV cost of Fig 8, Transformer with GQA
results.quote: For example, YOCO can serve 128K tokens with 1GB GPU memory, while Transformer with GQA [ALTdJ+23] can only support 1.6K tokens at 65B model size.

results.claim: Baseline problem: a 65B model's 512K-token KV cache is about 86GB.
results.setup: 65B, grouped-query attention, 8-bit KV quantization; H100-80GB capacity
results.quote: 512K tokens occupy about 86GB GPU memory, which is even larger than the capacity of one H100-80GB GPU.

results.claim: Baseline problem: 7B model prefill takes about 110 s for 450K tokens and 380 s for 1M on four H100s.
results.setup: 7B, Flash-Decoding and kernel fusion, four H100 GPUs
results.note: Sec 4.4 says Transformer needs about 180 s at 512K and 300 s at 1M (3B config); different models
results.quote: using four H100 GPUs, the 7B language model (augmented with Flash-Decoding [DHMS23] and kernel fusion) requires about 110 seconds to prefill 450K tokens, and 380 seconds for 1M length.

results.claim: YOCO-3B at 1.6T tokens reaches an Eval Harness zero-shot average of 0.636.
results.setup: 3B, 1.6T tokens, zero-shot LM Eval Harness over 8 tasks; StableLM-3B-4E1T has no printed average

results.claim: YOCO-3B at 1T tokens reaches an average of 0.634 vs OpenLLaMA-3B-v2 0.619 and StableLM-base-alpha-3B-v2 0.612.
YOCO-3B-1M after context extension averages 0.645 on Eval Harness.
YOCO-3B-1M multi-needle accuracy at 128K length: N=1 0.98, N=2 0.98, N=4 0.84, N=8 0.56.
results.setup: 128K length; 10 runs at the same depth and length averaged; compared to LWM-1M-text 7B (0.62 at N=8), MiniCPM-128K (0.56), ChatGLM3-128K (0.44), YaRN-Mistral-128K (0.20)

results.claim: YOCO-3B-1M passes single-needle retrieval across 1M context with near perfect accuracy.
results.setup: YOCO-3B-1M, needle city with magic number, 10 runs per depth/length, no long-instruction data

results.claim: Scaling curves 160M to 13B: YOCO-gRet validation loss beats Transformer and YOCO-SWA.
results.setup: Llama-style Transformer vs YOCO-gRet and YOCO-SWA (window 1,024), 10B tokens each, 2k seq length, validation loss (Fig 4, values not printed in text)

results.claim: 160M-model validation perplexity: YOCO-gRet 3.530, YOCO-SWA 3.553, Transformer 3.564, Mamba 3.645.
results.table: Table 8, row YOCOgRet, column Valid. Set

limits: Trained from scratch only; converting an existing Transformer is not shown.
The 65B KV saving is the per-token ratio from Fig 8, not a measured 65B run.
Profiling uses a 3B model; GPU count and batch size for profiling are not stated and Transformer memory at 1M (about 9.4x of 12.4GB) exceeds one 80GB card.
No seeds, no variance, no compute or hardware for training stated.
Self-decoder still keeps a constant-size cache (footnote 2).
Quality at scale compared on Eval Harness averages and validation loss only; multi-needle at N=8 is 0.56, below LWM-1M-text (0.62).
Figure values (scaling-loss curves, throughput bars) are only in figures.
